clue.text: One in pokey with excellent natter

parts.note: someone locked up in the pokey, slang for prison, is a con, short for convict
fab is informal shorthand for fabulous, meaning excellent

explanation.surface: A prisoner and a splendid cellmate pass the time chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab is an informal chat, short for confabulation, just as a natter is a gossipy talk.

clue.text: Old noble restricts Newton's introduction?

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so the noble encloses the other piece

parts.note: a peer is a noble, a member of the peerage
N is the symbol for the newton, the SI unit of force

explanation.surface: An aristocrat of the past keeps a lid on Isaac Newton's preface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' reads as the scientist, but it is the unit of force, symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener is something that starts proceedings, such as an opening remark or first item, so an introduction.

clue.text: Select kitty's display container

parts.note: the flower of something is its choicest part, the select few
a kitty is a pool of money, also called the pot

explanation.surface: Choose the cat's show box.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerpot is a container in which plants are grown and put on display.

clue.text: Social event can end horribly with pub first

indicators.note: first says the pub goes at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a bar is a pub, or the counter in one

indicators.note: horribly says the letters are mangled into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A night out can finish badly when it starts at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn dance is a country gathering with folk dancing, a type of social event.

clue.text: As paper's fake this isn't printed

parts.note: paper, as in tissue, is soft, so 'as paper is' gives the adjective soft
a fake is a copy of the genuine article

explanation.surface: A remark that a forged document never went through the printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: The contrast is with 'hard copy', the printed version on paper; this kind exists only on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft copy is the electronic version of a document, viewed on screen rather than printed out.

clue.text: Pay off, for example including time is fine

indicators.note: one piece including others means it wraps around them

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example
f is the pencil grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Settling a debt is fine, for example, if it is done on time.
explanation.walkthrough: T, IS and F go inside SAY after its A: SA-TISF-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a debt or creditor is to pay what is owed in full, settling the account.

clue.text: Plants current Duke relocated away from the Sunshine State

indicators.note: moving away from somewhere means leaving it, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: Florida is nicknamed the Sunshine State
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Greenery and electricity follow an aristocrat who has left Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: I and D are taken out of FLORIDA, leaving FLORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plant life of a region.

clue.text: Conservative girl showing style

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A Tory young woman demonstrating elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Class means stylish excellence or elegance, as in a player with real class.

clue.text: Top after tug o' war's won, I suppose

definitions.meaning: a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a sweater

definitions.text: after tug o' war's won, I suppose
definitions.meaning: once one side wins a tug o' war, the pulling is finished

explanation.surface: A sweater is the prize once the rope contest is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a knitted jumper, and the phrase also reads as the moment the pull is over.

clue.text: Protest about pest — a politician

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or rally
c, for circa, is the abbreviation for about
a rat is a vermin pest, or a pestilent person

explanation.surface: A complaint about vermin, voiced by someone in public office.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, so a kind of politician.

clue.text: Sibyl, say, is one who couldn't possibly err

definitions.meaning: the sibyls were prophetesses of the ancient world who spoke the gods' answers
someone treated as an infallible authority whose word is never wrong

explanation.definitionFit: The Sibyls were prophetic priestesses, and the word also means any person regarded as an infallible source of wisdom.

clue.text: Rely on one of a pair leaving cunning finish

indicators.note: one piece leaving another means it is dropped from that word

parts.note: deep can mean crafty, as in a deep one who hides his schemes
the word for cunning has two of the same vowel side by side, and one of that pair goes
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: An instruction about a twin departing before a crafty conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops one of the two Es from DEEP, giving DEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to trust and lean on them, the same as relying on them.

clue.text: Covers will be pulled back getting spicy pic

indicators.note: pulled back says the letters of the covering word run in reverse order

parts.note: a bridge spans or covers a gap, so covers means spans
spicy food is hot

explanation.surface: Bedclothes are about to be whipped off to reveal a racy photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be pulled back' turns SPANS into SNAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick informal photograph, and pic is casual shorthand for picture.

clue.text: Swing hammer

definitions.meaning: to swing a camera horizontally across a scene
to hammer a play or film is to slate it in a review

explanation.definitionFit: Pan means both to sweep a camera sideways and to criticise something severely.

clue.text: Skinflint Quaker, then unknown, with appropriate queen

parts.note: William Penn, founder of Pennsylvania, was a famous Quaker
y is one of the letters used for an unknown in algebra
to appropriate something is to pinch, or steal, it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A list of characters: a member of the Society of Friends, a mystery figure and a fitting royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny-pincher is a miser who hates spending, a synonym for a skinflint.

clue.text: A gent line dancing is ungainly

indicators.note: words that are dancing jig about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man in a line dance moves clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or polish, close to ungainly or awkward.

clue.text: Confess to fair approach initially

indicators.note: initially says this piece comes first, at the start of the answer

parts.note: to come is to approach
a fair fight or fair copy is a clean one

explanation.surface: Owning up to a just way of tackling things at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is the idiom for owning up and telling the truth about something hidden.

clue.text: Cold break touring a grand valley?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

indicators.note: to tour something is to go around it, so the break wraps the other pieces

parts.note: leave is a break from work, a holiday
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A chilly holiday going around a big valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A and G go inside LEAVE: LEAV-AG-E. The question mark flags the playful definition: a cleavage is the valley between breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleavage is the hollow between a woman's breasts, likened here to a valley between hills.

clue.text: Twit cremated fancy teatime treat?

parts.note: a clot is a fool, the same as a twit

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests elaborate reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool has been cremated in some extravagant fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted cream is the thick cream served with scones in a Devon or Cornish cream tea, hence a teatime treat.

clue.text: Jack to blacken tea urn in odd spots

indicators.note: the letters in the odd-numbered positions are taken

explanation.surface: A sailor spoils his drink by dirtying the urn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to blacken' is a second definition: to tar is to coat in black pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack and tar are both old informal names for a sailor.

clue.text: Maritime redundancy means reduced cover above

definitions.meaning: a cut in the ship's personnel, the sailors laid off
hair cropped very short covers the head only thinly

explanation.surface: Job losses at sea lead to a closely trimmed haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crewcut is a very short haircut, and read literally it is a reduction in a ship's company.

clue.text: 'Arsh time in 'Ackney fire

parts.note: a Cockney dropping the h says 'arsh for harsh, a near synonym of hard, likewise said without its h
Hackney is in London's East End, where a Cockney drops the h of hour

explanation.surface: Cockney passion: a hard hour spent in Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes mark dropped Hs in a Cockney accent: HARD loses its H and so does HOUR. Hackney is a borough of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate enthusiasm, the fire of strong feeling.

clue.text: Fashion industry vogue is full of old jazz

indicators.note: one word being full of another means the second sits inside the first

parts.note: something all the rage is in vogue, so rage means vogue
trad is traditional jazz, the old New Orleans style

explanation.surface: A fashionable style brimming with vintage jazz music.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD goes inside RAGE after its G: RAG-TRAD-E.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is informal British slang for the clothing and fashion business.

clue.text: Five shots of Absolut on ice with …

indicators.note: five letters are drawn out of the words that follow, a run hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Pouring a vodka over ice and topping it up with a mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: Absolut is a brand of vodka; the trailing dots leave the solver to supply the familiar vodka and tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is the mixer that typically goes with a spirit such as vodka or gin.

clue.text: The prime from Aeschylus' characters?

definitions.meaning: the Greek playwright wrote in the Greek alphabet, whose first letter this is

explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet and so denotes whatever is first or foremost.

clue.text: Euphemistically I could offer a loose corset

definitions.text: Euphemistically I could offer a loose corset

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters are freed and set down in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone coyly hinting at the services on offer, including slackened underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges CORSET; the whole clue is a sly description of a paid companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Escort is a polite euphemism for someone paid for companionship, often of a sexual kind.

clue.text: Laidback worker getting in better forty winks

indicators.note: one piece getting in another means it goes inside it

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: laid back read literally means turned backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the ant is the classic crossword worker insect

explanation.surface: A relaxed employee finds a way of going one up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laidback' turns ANT into TNA, and 'getting in' puts it inside CAP after the A: CA-TNA-P.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light sleep, and forty winks is the idiom for a brief doze.

clue.text: Guardian and char open dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper and a cleaning lady are set wide apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies and protects a young person in public, acting as a guardian.

clue.text: Broker around Marseille sea song

parts.note: near Marseille French is spoken, and the French word for sea is mer
a chant is a simple song, as in plainchant

explanation.surface: A trader somewhere on the Mediterranean coast singing a shanty.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a trader who buys and sells goods, a broker in the sense of a middleman.

clue.text: A stretch of fat, undramatic Russian countryside?

indicators.note: A stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dull, broad expanse of land somewhere in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless Arctic plain covering much of northern Russia.
